finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: An attacker can input a value that causes an integer overflow when stored in a 64-bit integer, leading to undefined behavior.
finding.assumptions: The input is not properly bounds-checked before being stored in 'value'.

parsed.refutation_attempt: 1. Checked for buffer bounds: the call to scanf on line 8 reads a single 64‑bit integer into the variable ‘value’, which is a scalar and not a buffer. 2. Confirmed that SCNd64 expands to a format specifier that matches the type of the target pointer (int64_t *), so no type mismatch can cause a write past the variable’s boundary. 3. Reviewed standard behavior: if the input number is out of range for int64_t, the result is implementation‑defined (usually the value is clamped or an error is set), but this does not constitute a buffer overflow. 4. No other code paths or checks affect this input handling, so no buffer overflow path exists.
